topic: Research: Microsoft Work IQ APIs GA June 16, 2026: Developer Guide to Enterprise AI Workflow Automation
keyword: Microsoft Work IQ APIs GA developer guide

key_points: Official Microsoft 365 announcement says Work IQ APIs will be generally available on June 16, 2026.
Positions Work IQ as the best API surface for agents to interact with Microsoft 365 data and apps.
Explains that Work IQ provides business context from email, calendar, meetings, chats, files, people, collaboration patterns, and line-of-business systems.
Introduces consumption-based pricing in Copilot Credits with fixed Tool costs and variable Chat/Context costs.
Highlights new Microsoft 365 admin center controls for billing, spend policies, usage limits, alerts, and cost monitoring.
Developer-focused announcement frames Work IQ as production-ready intelligence for agents rather than individual users.
Confirms GA endpoints on June 16, 2026: Agent-to-Agent (A2A), redesigned remote MCP server, and REST API.
States usage is independent of Microsoft 365 Copilot licensing and available on a consumption basis.
Emphasizes enterprise governance and cost management controls in the Microsoft 365 admin center.
Directs developers to the public preview GitHub resources for hands-on evaluation before GA.
Microsoft Learn overview defines Work IQ API as an agentic API for securely reasoning over Microsoft 365 data.
Explains that existing permissions, compliance, and governance controls are preserved.
Documents three integration styles: A2A, MCP, and REST.
Frames Work IQ as a higher-level alternative to manually stitching Microsoft 365 context through lower-level APIs.
Useful for implementation details, prerequisites, authentication, and protocol selection.
Third-party hands-on walkthrough targeting day-one GA implementers.
Compares Work IQ with Microsoft Graph and argues Work IQ is a different API shape focused on pre-digested, permission-trimmed context.
Covers admin consent, user setup, Copilot Credits, and example apps.
Includes practical setup pitfalls such as admin consent and AADSTS650052-style errors.
Good competitor for searchers looking for a plain-English developer walkthrough.
SEO-oriented article focused on using Work IQ to access Microsoft 365 context through agent tools.
Emphasizes the June 16 GA date and the launch of A2A endpoints, remote MCP server, and REST API.
Frames the key developer question as whether Work IQ can replace custom Microsoft Graph plus retrieval pipelines for agent use cases.

Useful to benchmark keyword coverage around Microsoft 365 agents, MCP, A2A, and Graph alternatives.

stats.fact: Work IQ APIs are scheduled for general availability on June 16, 2026, after the June 2, 2026 Microsoft announcement.
At GA, Microsoft says Work IQ API endpoints will include A2A, a redesigned remote MCP server, and a REST API.
Work IQ API supports multiple protocols for agents: Agent-to-Agent (A2A), Model Context Protocol (MCP), and REST.
Microsoft's licensing page says Work IQ API has no separate subscription, SKU, or per-user license; charges draw down Copilot Credits.

Microsoft's licensing example lists the static Work IQ Tool API at 0.1 Copilot Credits per API call, with example scenario pricing ranges from about $0.20-$1.50 per call depending on scenario complexity.
Copilot Studio capacity packs are listed at 25,000 Copilot Credits for $200 per pack per month, providing a rough public anchor for Copilot Credit economics.
Microsoft's 2026 Work Trend Index is based on trillions of anonymized Microsoft 365 productivity signals and a survey of 20,000 AI-using workers across 10 countries.
Gartner predicted that 40% of enterprise applications will include task-specific AI agents by the end of 2026, up from less than 5% in 2025.
Gartner's 2026 agentic AI hype-cycle coverage says only 17% of organizations have deployed AI agents so far, while more than 60% expect to do so within two years.
Microsoft Partner coverage of the 2026 Work Trend Index says agents in the Microsoft 365 ecosystem increased 15x year over year and 18x in large enterprises.

angles: Developer guide angle: Work IQ is not just another Microsoft Graph wrapper; it is an agent-oriented context and action layer that returns synthesized, permission-aware work intelligence.
Protocol-choice angle: explain when to use A2A, MCP, or REST based on whether the caller is an autonomous agent, a coding assistant/tool host, or a traditional app/service.
Governance angle: the GA story is as much about tenant billing, spend policy, admin consent, and permission trimming as it is about new endpoints.
Cost-model angle: Work IQ changes Microsoft 365 agent architecture from license-only planning to Copilot Credit consumption modeling and per-scenario budgeting.
Architecture migration angle: compare Work IQ with existing Microsoft Graph plus search/RAG pipelines and show where each still belongs.
Enterprise workflow automation angle: focus examples on meeting follow-ups, account research, project status synthesis, compliance-aware knowledge retrieval, and manager task rollups.
Pre-GA caution angle: as of June 13, 2026, GA is scheduled for June 16, so developers should verify endpoint docs, pricing tables, and tenant controls on or after launch day.

Security angle: Work IQ honors Microsoft 365 permissions, sensitivity labels, and tenant governance, but developers still need app registration, delegated permissions, consent, logs, and budget guardrails.
